html:
Fado is a style of Portuguese song, usually sad, sung by one voice with the Portuguese guitar and the classical guitar. It arose in the poor districts of Lisbon in the early 1800s.

Its theme is saudade, a longing for something lost or absent: a lover, a home, the sea. It was first sung in taverns and brothels of the Alfama and Mouraria districts. Coimbra developed its own fado, sung by students of the university.

In the 20th century Amália Rodrigues made fado famous around the world. The Salazar regime promoted it as a national music, which made it suspect for a time after 1974. A new generation revived it, and UNESCO listed it as world heritage in 2011. See Portugal.
sum: Fado is a style of Portuguese song, usually sad, sung by one voice with the Portuguese guitar and the classical guitar. It arose in the poor districts of Lisbon in the early 1800s.
